3.0.3: Firefox's own pages, like Settings and the Protections Dashboard, now use Fjord's blue instead of Firefox's purple, with Fjord's shield and logo.
Settings no longer show Firefox Labs or Mozilla's Sync, which Fjord doesn't use. Fjord syncs on its own, in Fjord's settings.
3.0.2: New tab: 48 new photos, from coral reefs and sea turtles to cars, waves, deserts, wildlife and city skylines, and every photo is now sharper. Fjord fetches the new versions once, in the background.
YouTube: one click in or out of the private player, with the button in the address bar: “Watch privately” on YouTube, “Open on YouTube” in the player.
Popped-out videos have a pin at the top right: keep them on top of other windows, or let them go behind. The pop-out button and the full-screen notice now look like the rest of Fjord.
The “What’s new” window after an update fits on any screen, however many updates it covers.
3.0.1: Windows: a new installer in Fjord's look. It can't be closed halfway through, retries a download that stalls, and tells you clearly if something went wrong.
Windows: uninstalling closes Fjord for you if it's open, lets you choose whether to keep your bookmarks and passwords, and removes every shortcut and every trace of Fjord in Windows' settings.
3.0.0: Calm web: besides ads and trackers, Fjord now takes out what pages use to pressure you: fake urgency like “Only 2 left”, countdowns next to offers, guilt-trip buttons, email and chat pop-ups, and videos that play on their own. Turn it off for one site in Shields, or everywhere in Settings › Calm web.

Sync through a folder you already have, like iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive or a USB stick, not just over your home Wi-Fi. Each device writes its own encrypted file, so the folder only ever holds scrambled data. Passwords and settings now sync between your computers too. Still no account and no server.
New tab: a picture of your own instead of the landscapes, in Settings › New tab.
Tab folders in Fjord's look, and they work with Spaces.
A new first-time setup, and redesigned Settings where every section scrolls all the way down.
Fjord is called Fjord, not Firefox, when you make it your default browser, and starts without Firefox's loading screen.
The Mozilla account sign-in is gone from the menu: Fjord doesn't send your data anywhere.
2.0.0: Split view: two tabs side by side. Right-click a tab or a link, or press Ctrl+K (⌘K on a Mac) and choose Split view. A split works across Spaces and keeps its two tabs together.
Memory saver shows what it freed: Settings › Performance says how many tabs are asleep and about how much memory that saved, and so does a sleeping tab when you hover over it.
1.0.8: Sync with your iPhone: scan a QR code in Settings with Fjord for iPhone, and your history, bookmarks and open tabs go both ways over your home Wi-Fi. Nothing goes through the internet.
Spaces: separate sets of tabs like Work and Personal, each with its own colour. The button at the start of the tabs switches between them.
Privacy report in Settings: what Fjord blocked each day this week, which companies tried to track you and on which sites. It stays on this computer.
24 new photos on the new tab.
Windows: no more stray “Fjord Private Browsing” shortcut in the Start menu.
1.0.7: Mac: Fjord.dmg opens a small window that shows you to drag Fjord into Applications.
Mac: Fjord starts with its own icon instead of Firefox's, and macOS no longer warns that Fjord tried to read another app's data.
1.0.6: Private YouTube player: videos play on their own, without recommendations or your YouTube history. Turn it on the first time you watch something, or in Privacy.
Randomised fingerprint: every site gets slightly different canvas, WebGL and audio readings, so sites can't use them to recognise you.
Hide parts of pages: right-click a cookie wall, sidebar or pop-up and choose “Hide this”. Shields can show it again.
Command bar: Ctrl+K (⌘K on a Mac) finds your tabs, bookmarks, history and Fjord's actions.
Link preview: Shift-click a link to open it over the page.
1.0.5: After an update, Fjord tells you what's new, like this.
Forget this site: one click in Shields deletes a site's cookies, saved data and history.
Reader view in Fjord's font and colours.
Linux on ARM computers, with its own download.
